name: edgepad
description: Use an Android phone as a Bluetooth trackpad, media remote and control panel for a Windows laptop. Corner dials, multi-finger gestures, on-screen keyboard and gamepad. No account, no server, no telemetry.

paragraphs: Edgepad turns an Android phone into a trackpad, a media remote and a control panel for a Windows laptop or a Mac, over a direct Bluetooth link with nothing in between.
The phone's screen. The finger crosses the trackpad, then slides the corner ruler and the volume follows.

It is for the times the laptop is across the room rather than under your hands: plugged into a television, docked on a desk you are not sitting at, parked somewhere a mouse dongle will not reach. The alternatives are a remote app that only sends media keys, or a remote-desktop app that streams the whole screen and wants an account and a network round trip to change the volume. Edgepad is neither. The phone and the laptop pair once, the way a headset does, and after that they talk directly: no account, no Wi-Fi, no service in between that can be slow or down. whatItDoes.text: Edgepad turns an Android phone into a trackpad, a media remote and a control panel for a Windows laptop or a Mac, over a direct Bluetooth link with nothing in between.

requirements.text: The phone and the laptop pair once, the way a headset does, and after that they talk directly: no account, no Wi-Fi, no service in between that can be slow or down.
The cost is Bluetooth's own — both ends need it, and it does not reach another room or the internet.

The menu shows whether a phone is connected, then Update available when a newer release exists, Start at login, Open log, Documentation, Forget trusted phone and Quit Edgepad, with the version beside it.
